decisions.detail: QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` defaults to off. ... `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is also off by default (`mbedtls_config.h:2196`). | WHY: The answer names both MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the macros that gate the threading code, and says the library's mutexes sit behind the first one. || QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` defaults to off. ... `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is also off by default (`mbedtls_config.h:2196`). | WHY: The answer names both MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the macros controlling threading and gating the locks. || QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` defaults to off. ... `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is also off by default (`mbedtls_config.h:2196`). | WHY: The answer names both MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the macros controlling the threading/locking code, and it says the library's mutexes sit behind the MBEDTLS_THREADING_C gate.

decisions.mark: states that the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves BOTH threading macros undefined, so a default build defines neither
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` defaults to off... `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is also off by default (`mbedtls_config.h:2196`)... The index also reports no definition site for `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`, so the "off" reading likely comes from a commented-out `#define`. Confirm against the header." | WHY: The answer states that both threading macros are off by default in the shipped mbedtls_config.h, so a default build defines neither. The hedge about confirming against the header doesn't remove that claim. || QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` defaults to off... `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is also off by default (`mbedtls_config.h:2196`)... so the "off" reading likely comes from a commented-out `#define`. Confirm against the header." | WHY: The answer says both threading macros are off by default in the shipped mbedtls_config.h, so a default build defines neither. It hedges on the commented-out `#define` but still states the substance.

decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "The library itself spawns nothing." and "The mutexes are global objects in `library/threading.c` with `MUTEX_INIT`" (also: "The library reaches it through the `mbedtls_mutex_lock` function pointer") | WHY: The answer says the library creates no threads, and it also says `library/threading.c` supplies the mutex abstraction that threaded callers use. || QUOTE: "The only spawn in the index that touches shared state is the per-connection pthread server. It is a sample program, not library code. The library itself spawns nothing." and "The mutexes are global objects in `library/threading.c` with `MUTEX_INIT`" | WHY: The answer says the library spawns no threads and that `library/threading.c` supplies the mutex layer, which many library modules use through `mbedtls_mutex_lock`. || QUOTE: "The library itself spawns nothing." and "The mutexes are global objects in `library/threading.c` with `MUTEX_INIT`" | WHY: The answer states that the library spawns no threads (only sample programs do) and that library/threading.c supplies the mutex abstraction (`mbedtls_mutex_lock`, global mutexes) used when threading is enabled.
